title: Pointer Misuse
problem: Fix the pointer dereference so the program prints the value 42. The pointer is declared but never assigned.
starterCode:
#include <stdio.h>
int main(){ int x = 42; int *p; printf("%d\n", *p); return 0; }

title: Array Index Overflow
problem: The code writes beyond array bounds and reads the wrong element. Fix it so it safely prints the last element (value 3) of the array.
starterCode:
#include <stdio.h>
int main(){ int a[3] = {1, 2, 3}; a[3] = 4; printf("%d\n", a[3]); return 0; }

title: Wrong Format Specifier
problem: The program uses the wrong format specifier. Fix printf so it correctly prints the integer 100.
starterCode:
#include <stdio.h>
int main(){ int x = 100; printf("%s\n", x); return 0; }
